carbon_low_alloy.general_corrosion: Requires corrosion protection in most atmospheric service; bare carbon/low-alloy steel is susceptible to general corrosion.
carbon_low_alloy.chlorides: Chloride/moisture environments accelerate corrosion; coatings, material upgrade or controlled environment may be required.
carbon_low_alloy.SCC: Environment and stress dependent; do not infer immunity from generic grade designation.
carbon_low_alloy.hydrogen: Hydrogen-assisted cracking can be relevant in high-strength/heat-treated conditions and certain charging/plating environments.
carbon_low_alloy.galvanic: Can act anodically when coupled to more noble metals in an electrolyte.

austenitic_stainless.general_corrosion: Good general atmospheric corrosion resistance; performance is environment dependent.
austenitic_stainless.chlorides: Pitting/crevice corrosion can govern in chloride environments. 316L generally offers better chloride resistance than 304; this is not an absolute service guarantee.
austenitic_stainless.SCC: Chloride stress-corrosion cracking is a known concern, particularly at elevated temperature and tensile stress.
austenitic_stainless.hydrogen: Hydrogen effects depend on grade, microstructure, charging condition and stress state; assess where service warrants.
austenitic_stainless.galvanic: Galvanic coupling requires electrolyte, area ratio and potential considerations.

martensitic_stainless.general_corrosion: Corrosion resistance is generally below low-carbon austenitic grades and depends strongly on heat treatment and surface condition.
martensitic_stainless.chlorides: Pitting/crevice corrosion remains possible; chloride service requires grade- and condition-specific assessment.
martensitic_stainless.SCC: Stress/environment interactions can be significant; heat treatment and hardness matter.
martensitic_stainless.hydrogen: Higher-strength/harder conditions can be susceptible to hydrogen-assisted cracking under appropriate charging and stress.
martensitic_stainless.galvanic: Assess galvanic coupling when paired with more noble alloys.

precipitation_hardening_stainless.general_corrosion: Good corrosion resistance relative to many hardenable steels, but strongly dependent on condition, microstructure and environment.
precipitation_hardening_stainless.chlorides: Pitting/crevice corrosion and localized attack must be considered in chloride service.
precipitation_hardening_stainless.SCC: Condition, strength level, environment and residual/applied stress can materially affect SCC performance.
precipitation_hardening_stainless.hydrogen: High-strength conditions require consideration of hydrogen-assisted cracking where charging is possible.
precipitation_hardening_stainless.galvanic: Coupling to dissimilar metals should be assessed for electrolyte exposure.

tool_steel.general_corrosion: Not selected primarily for corrosion resistance; protect in corrosive service.
tool_steel.chlorides: Chloride/moisture exposure can cause corrosion; surface treatment/protection may be required.
tool_steel.SCC: Assess only against the actual service environment and heat-treated condition.
tool_steel.hydrogen: Hydrogen effects can be relevant in hardened high-strength tooling/service conditions.
tool_steel.galvanic: Assess with dissimilar metallic couples in wet environments.

ferritic_stainless.general_corrosion: Moderate general corrosion resistance with strong dependence on surface condition and environment.
ferritic_stainless.chlorides: Localized chloride corrosion remains possible and should not be treated as immune.
ferritic_stainless.SCC: Generally less susceptible to classic chloride SCC than austenitic stainless steels, but service-specific assessment remains required.
ferritic_stainless.hydrogen: Consider charging and stress conditions where high consequence exists.
